opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049) is a full-time Analyst. Requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is the maximum level for non-owners of the system; the request is at the maximum and is approved.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Recommended level: read.
reason: There is a conflict between the two notes: HR note describes John Rodriguez (E049) as a full-time Analyst, while the Security DB note describes him as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read and can never have admin. Since employment/security DB evidence indicates contractor status, the maximum allowed level is read, and the requested write exceeds it. Granting the maximum (read) is the safe determination.
